    Q3 In Review: Pay TV Shrinks, Streaming And Sports Step Up

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (739 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Adexchanger

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Have you been keeping up with the quarterly earnings scoreboard for media and entertainment companies?
    • In a recent development, it’s a lot, we know.
    • Before you hunker down for Turkey Day, here’s a rundown on the TV and streaming companies (those that remain after all the recent consolidation, that is) that posted their earnings for the three months ending on Sept.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Have you been keeping up with the quarterly earnings scoreboard for media and entertainment companies?

    In a recent development, it’s a lot, we know. Not to worry. We figured you’d be busy, and so we tuned in to Q3 call after Q3 call so you didn’t have to. (You’re welcome.).

    Before you hunker down for Turkey Day, here’s a rundown on the TV and streaming companies (those that remain after all the recent consolidation, that is) that posted their earnings for the three months ending on Sept. 30 – and what these reports reveal about the state of TV and media today.

    Netflix’s Q3 numbers look decent on paper. Revenue rose 12% year over year to $12.9 billion, while advertising revenue alone has spiked over 80% this year. But Netflix wasn’t able to double its ad revenue again this year as planned. To be fair, growing ad revenue rapidly was easier to do back when Netflix first started its ads biz from scratch.

    On the advertising front, Netflix also touted improved programmatic targeting and ad measurement capabilities, including a pixel to measure conversions.

    Comcast’s media division reported $5.4 billion in earnings last quarter, a 13% YOY jump from this time last year. Alongside NBCUniversal, which Comcast plans to spin off as a standalone company alongside British broadcaster Sky, Comcast’s media division also includes NBCU’s Peacock, Telemundo, Bravo and Universal film and television studios.

    It has been revealed that but Comcast had weaker performance across the broadband and theme park sides of the business, which saw a 6.1% revenue decline. (The theme parks live under the Universal brand and will go with NBCU and Sky in the spin-off.).

    Unlike Netflix, Fox boasted of recent boosts in engagement. Its free ad-supported TV platform, Tubi, saw a 23% YOY increase in viewing hours, thanks in part to the platform’s recent focus on creator content.

    Zooming out from Tubi, Fox’s overall revenue rose 22% to $4.6 billion last quarter, including a 47% jump in advertising revenue. But, sports and streaming aside, it wasn’t all sunshine and rainbows. Fox News saw major viewership declines throughout the year and into October, when total-day ratings fell 27% ahead of the midterms.

    Fox was vague about details regarding its acquisition of Roku but asserted it expects to close the deal soon. A mere few days later, on Nov. 6, Fox unveiled it officially completed the acquisition.

    Versant Media, which spun off from Comcast in January, posted a 4% decline in Q3 revenue, a loss it mostly blamed on secular declines in the pay-TV industry.

    Versant also closed its acquisition of Full Swing last quarter, a deal that supports its ambitions to lean on live sports – golf in particular – as a competitive advantage.

    Industry observers note that skydance closed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on Oct. 4, so there were no WBD-specific numbers in its Q3 report. But WBD aside, Skydance reported $7 billion in revenue last quarter, representing 5% YOY growth.

    Recent findings suggest that streaming was a highlight, with Paramount+ revenue jumping 21% YOY to just over $2.1 billion. Skydance also announced plans to launch a service combining HBO Max and Paramount+ at the beginning of next year.

    Skydance CEO David Ellison confirmed that Paramount+ and Pluto are officially operating on the same ad tech stack, noting that integrating HBO Max should be a relatively speedy process.

    Disney reported a 16% revenue jump to $25.9 billion in Q4 (its fiscal year ends in September) and a revenue increase of 8% to $102.3 billion for the full year.

    Ad revenue grew 10% to $1.7 billion within Disney’s entertainment segment. For its sports segment, that growth rate was 20%.

    Industry observers note that disney also shared that it’s unifying Disney+ and Hulu into one app beginning next month. The organization will add more sports to Disney+ in December and introduce creator content from TikTok into the Disney+ mobile app.

    Sports streamer Fubo, which also ends its fiscal year in September, saw its fourth-quarter revenue inch up to $1.5 billion from $1.48 billion during the same period last year.

    But Fubo suffered a net loss of $51.8 million in its Q4 – a heavier loss than the $38.8 million it posted in the same quarter last year. Fubo attributed the loss to operational and restructuring costs related to its recent merger with Hulu + Live TV.

    Thanks for reading and happy streaming!

    In a recent development, we use Outlook at AdExchanger, and last Wednesday everything came crashing down. PR people resorted to frantic texts to reach journalists. No emails showed up in my inbox for 18 hours. But ad tech soldiered on. We open the episode with a check-in about last week’s historic outage and some of the surprising takeaways for ad tech from this flurry of outages.

    Then, what do we know about the state of the growing app economy? Liftoff and AppLovin both held their earnings calls in recent weeks, and the app-focused ad tech platforms are painting a rosy picture compared to The Trade Desk – though The Trade Desk is also seeing growing mobile spend. Plus, compared to TV, ad units on mobile apps go for a fraction of the price.

    Sources indicate that but mobile app advertising remains very much a closed ecosystem, with ads on apps showing ads for apps. AdExchanger Senior Editor James Hercher, who covered all of these earnings, shares his mobile app outlook and how our listeners should think about the opportunity in this growing space.

    Finally, do you have your Christmas decorations out yet? Have you added your email address to any “early Cyber Week” notifications? Retailers are out in force, offering early Black Friday sales or semi-gated access to Cyber Week discounts. With a mere 29 days between Thanksgiving and Christmas, we’ll talk about how brands are starting earlier with the holiday deals, with Senior Editor Victoria McNally. If you’re not into Christmas shopping starting earlier, does that make you a Grinch?

    #112801. Tech Report: Ampersand Is Offloading Its Indie Agency Business To Comcast And Spectrum Following Mass Layoffs

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (700 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Adexchanger ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Ampersand Is Offloading Its Indie Agency Business To Comcast And Spectrum Following Mass Layoffs

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (700 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Adexchanger

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bridging the gap between linear TV and streaming is apparently easier mentioned than done.
    • Ampersand, a TV ad platform that combines linear and streaming data from national and local markets to unify audience targeting and measurement, is significantly paring back its business, AdExchanger has learned.
    • The company, a joint venture established in 2019 by Comcast, Charter and Cox (which Charter now owns), will offload its independent agency business to Comcast Advertising and Charter’s Spectrum Reach in 2027.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Bridging the gap between linear TV and streaming is apparently easier mentioned than done.

    Ampersand, a TV ad platform that combines linear and streaming data from national and local markets to unify audience targeting and measurement, is significantly paring back its business, AdExchanger has learned.

    The company, a joint venture established in 2019 by Comcast, Charter and Cox (which Charter now owns), will offload its independent agency business to Comcast Advertising and Charter’s Spectrum Reach in 2027.

    Recent findings suggest that in October, Ampersand sent a memo to clients announcing the decision effective Jan. 1, an Ampersand spokesperson confirmed.

    Ampersand will continue operating, but with a focus on agency holding companies and political advertising.

    The decision comes on the heels of recent layoffs at Ampersand.

    Ampersand didn’t share more details with AdExchanger about the rationale behind its decision to hand off indie agency ad sales. But the client memo, which AdExchanger viewed, reveals some hints.

    Per the memo: “This new model will give independent agencies more direct access to Comcast Advertising and Spectrum Reach’s differentiated capabilities across premium video, streaming, data and technology, advanced audiences, measurement and attribution.”.

    To be fair, media buyers are increasingly seeking more direct access to TV and streaming inventory as they prioritize cost-cutting and ad performance. Indie agencies, it seems, would rather bypass Ampersand as their go-between and tap Comcast or Spectrum directly instead.

    The memo also suggests that indie agencies may value certain capabilities that are unique to Comcast and Spectrum’s ad tech stacks.

    Additionally, Ampersand specializes in local TV advertising. So, perhaps indie agencies are less interested in direct access to local TV inventory these days than, say, political advertisers are.

    Meanwhile, Ampersand has been struggling lately, at least judging by recent rounds of layoffs, which the tech giant did not publicly announce.

    There were several significant layoffs over the past year and change, a source with knowledge of Ampersand’s business told AdExchanger anonymously.

    Industry observers note that glassdoor reviews also indicate a bleak state of affairs, along with rumors of the company’s full shutdown. “There have been mass layoffs over the past two years,” a former Ampersand account executive wrote in October. “Most people expect the company to close in the next 2-3 years.”.

    AdExchanger first reached out to Ampersand after hearing rumors of a full shutdown from a source familiar with the company, but Ampersand denied these rumors and emphasized that it will continue to operate next year.

    Other Glassdoor reviews, however, are similarly pessimistic about the company’s long-term viability.

    Recent findings suggest that the current leadership is “driving the tech giant into extinction,” another account executive wrote in October while still employed at Ampersand. “Over the last few years, they have done little to develop or improve products or relationships. Instead, they have focused on reducing staff.”.

    Recent findings suggest that ampersand confirmed to AdExchanger that the decision to offload its indie agency business to Comcast and Spectrum have impacted roles, but declined to share specifics. Ampersand also acknowledged an unrelated round of layoffs in 2024.

    The future remains uncertain, but what’s clear is Ampersand’s ambitions to focus on reliable sources of TV ad demand: holdcos and political advertising. (And streaming, of course, because, well, duh.).

    In January, Ampersand debuted a newly introduced ad platform called TrueStream Political, aiming to help political advertisers more accurately reach voters across connected TV environments. Part of the platform’s pitch is its ability to reconcile audience and identity across disparate CTV platforms, a persistent challenge for CTV media buyers.

    Industry observers note that it makes sense for Ampersand to focus more on political ad buying. Political advertisers spent $12.06 billion leading up to the 2026 midterm elections, according to AdImpact, marking the first time a midterm cycle topped a presidential election in terms of ad spend.

    But although political advertising has seen a recent uptick during non-election years, it still tends to be very seasonal. You can, however, bank on a major influx of political ad dollars coming in roughly every two years.

    Sources indicate that so, sure, streaming and political are hot right now. But will this sharpened focus help Ampersand survive into the future? Well … stay tuned.

    As audiences turn to DMs and group chats to make purchase decisions, standard last-click platform reports miss authentic peer recommendations.

    In this episode of Inside the Stack, Snap’s Head of Performance Marketing GTM, Rick Lucas, and Kitsch CMO Ying Ying Kuang explain why last-click attribution—while still essential—isn’t the whole story.

    They discuss how Kitsch used a 16% geo-lift holdout test to prove Snap’s incremental value beyond the click, why Clicks + Deterministic Views (CDV) are necessary to capture real demand, and how to get comfortable living in the “messy middle” of continuous testing.

    As Netflix and Disney sniff around, YouTube hypes its creators’ “world-class, studio-quality” programming at L.A. Premieres event

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2496 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tonight, YouTube brought back its film-festival-style event, Creator Premieres, to showcase a fresh batch of “world-class, studio-quality creator programming” coming exclusively to its platform.
    • Last year’s Creator Premieres–the first YouTube held–took place at New York City’s historic screening space Metrograph and showed off projects from creators like Ms.
    • This year’s edition was hosted by House Guest‘s Scott Evans at The Hollywood Roosevelt in L.A., and highlighted upcoming projects from YouTube OGs and greats like Emma Chamberlain, Nick DiGiovanni, Lilly Singh, Wesley Wang, Grace Reiter, and more.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tonight, YouTube brought back its film-festival-style event, Creator Premieres, to showcase a fresh batch of “world-class, studio-quality creator programming” coming exclusively to its platform.

    Last year’s Creator Premieres–the first YouTube held–took place at New York City’s historic screening space Metrograph and showed off projects from creators like Ms. Rachel, Brave Wilderness, Dhar Mann, Deestroying, and Cleo Abram.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    This year’s edition was hosted by House Guest‘s Scott Evans at The Hollywood Roosevelt in L.A., and highlighted upcoming projects from YouTube OGs and greats like Emma Chamberlain, Nick DiGiovanni, Lilly Singh, Wesley Wang, Grace Reiter, and more.

    Google President Sean Downey took the stage to highlight YouTube’s continued dominance on TV screens, and gave a nod to participating creators for fueling the UGC machine that keeps viewers coming back to YouTube–on TVs and across other devices.

    Of course, he also appealed to advertisers in the same breath, reminding them that this “world-class” content is what they could be marketing alongside, if they cough up the cash to Google.

    Industry observers note that “YouTube creators are not just shaping modern culture, they are redefining the entire entertainment landscape. This slate of highlights demonstrates how creators are commanding primetime attention on the big screen and building unmatched fan loyalty,” Downey said. “For brands, this isn’t about buying thirty seconds of ad space; it’s about moving past standard commercial breaks and partnering directly with the storytellers who are defining modern culture.”.

    It has been revealed that youTube has spent years at the top of TV watch time charts–a fact that really gets under the skin of competitor Netflix. Up till recently, though, Netflix’s main response to this irritant was talking a lot of sh*t about YouTube and occasionally signing back catalog deals with view-drivers like Ms. Rachel and CoComelon.

    Recent findings suggest that but in the last 12 months, something’s shifted. Netflix has begun tapping creators like Salish Matter, Alan Chikin Chow, and the Stokes Twins not for back catalog agreements, but for development deals–deals which result in exclusive original programming that won’t appear on YouTube.

    It has been revealed that and YouTube’s not happy about it. The platform has been offering creators money, including production financing and sweet ad deals, in exchange for turning down offers from Netflix. Conversely, creators who decide to sign with Netflix are put on YouTube’s naughty list, and denied perks like revenue shares from primo ad deals.

    Industry observers note that (That being said, Netflix-friendly creators aren’t entirely blacklisted. DiGiovanni signed a catalog crossposting deal with Netflix in July, and was still one of the headline creators at tonight’s showcase.).

    The point we’re making here is this: With Netflix–and Disney–sniffing around, YouTube has more incentive than ever to hype up its creators and their projects on a big stage.

    So that’s exactly what it’s doing.

    Nick DiGiovanni | Chef | Upcoming series live now on a dedicated YouTube channel.

    Industry observers note that chef Nick DiGiovanni, the creator behind the world’s largest food YouTube channel, rolls out Chef (@Chef) – a new series from his production manufacturer, Knife Drop Studios. After reaching billions of viewers through his global culinary adventures (@NickDiGiovanni) and step-by-step recipes (@NicksKitchen), DiGiovanni is now turning the camera solely toward fellow professional chefs, offering an unfiltered look inside kitchens around the globe. From Michelin-starred restaurants and hidden street food gems showcased in full-length episodes, to POV recipes in short-form episodes, Chef puts viewers in the shoes of the people behind the scenes, offering a unique, captivating perspective for everyone from the culinary obsessed to the simply curious. You can view the first full-length episode, “Inside the World’s #1 Pizza Restaurant” now, only on YouTube, along with the first short-form POV episode, “Butter Chicken Shawarma”. New short-form POV episodes will debut daily across Nick’s newly-debuted @Chef channel with full-length episodes rolling out throughout 2026-27 exclusively on YouTube.

    According to recent reports, morgan Jay | Music Therapy with Morgan Jay | Latest series premieres Nov. 18 on Jay’s YouTube channel.

    Music Therapy is an original YouTube series developed and produced by viral comedian and musician Morgan Jay and Ty Stafford of Austin-based creative agency Hello Party, financed by Live Nation Studios. In each episode, Jay plays musical therapist to a celebrity guest, blending unscripted conversation and improv with live songwriting before the pair close with an original song they create together. The result lands somewhere between a talk show, a comedy special and a live concert. The first season features Kam Patterson, Ron Funches, Mara Wilson, Brennan Lee Mulligan, Yung Gravy, Matt Friend, Abbey Romeo, Mark Smalls, Tony Jefferson, ASHBY, Josh Johnson and Mandal Mann. Music Therapy was created by Morgan Jay and Ty Stafford (Hello Party) and is directed by Stafford. Brooke Schley serves as showrunner and co-writes the series with Jay. Executive producers are Graham Sicalowski, Robin Rapino, Stella Bulochnikov, Brooke Schley and Matt Sadeghian.

    It has been revealed that emma Chamberlain | What Are You Waiting For? | Newly introduced series premieres early 2027 on Chamberlain’s channel.

    According to recent reports, emma Chamberlain doesn’t like waiting in line – and wants to understand more about people who do. In this upcoming ongoing series, what starts as an investigation of New York City’s most frequented lines unspools into a thoughtful and expansive meditation on subcultures, fandoms, and what makes our modern world tick. At once whimsical, profound and provocative, and underpinned by Emma’s singular POV, What Are You Waiting For? is a hilarious cultural commentary that not only asks what people are waiting for – but why. The series is executive produced by two-time Emmy and Golden Globe winner Joe Lewis, with Amplify Pictures (Fleabag, 100 Foot Wave) serving as the co-studio and production organization.

    Industry observers note that grace Reiter | Twilight (but better) | New parody film premieres Feb. 18 on Reiter’s channel.

    Recent findings suggest that comedian, writer, and actor Grace Reiter (Saturday Night Live) is expanding her comedic universe with Twilight (but better), her second unscripted parody film. Reiter first made waves with her viral sketches and The Hunger Games (but better), which launched on YouTube in November 2025 and has garnered more than 18 million views. Now, alongside her work on SNL and her Netflix series Minimum Wage, Reiter brings her signature blend of spontaneous comedy, sharp satire, and irreverent humor to one of the most iconic franchises of a generation. Twilight (but better) is produced by But Better Productions. Grace Reiter serves as director with Andie Schlenker and Anderson Appleby as producers, and Cindy Schlenker as co-producer.

    Wesley Wang | Three newly introduced projects.

    Recent findings suggest that in this latest sci-fi horror short film, a routine welfare check at a remote desert preserve turns terrifying when four park rangers discover an otherworldly presence inside a woman’s tent, leaving the youngest ranger separated from his own body. Response is produced by Wesley Wang Media with Jason Rodelo serving as director and writer.

    Sources indicate that A new six-episode, interactive murder-mystery series that puts viewers in the role of detective, with $100,000 on the line for the first person to crack the case. Told through found footage, digital breadcrumbs and hidden clues woven throughout each episode, the mystery unfolds over six weeks on YouTube, challenging viewers to pause, rewind, decode and collaborate to uncover the truth. The first viewer to correctly solve the case wins $100,000! Extract 14 is directed and written by Wesley Wang and produced by Wesley Wang Media.

    According to recent reports, A new series where ten aspiring filmmakers, chosen from thousands of internet strangers, are brought to New York for an immersive, seven-day filmmaking bootcamp where they’ll compete for $100,000 to bring their dream movie to life. Guided by filmmaker Wesley Wang and a panel of Hollywood industry experts, contestants will take on every stage of the filmmaking process, culminating in a red carpet premiere where the viewers get the final say in choosing the grand prize winner. Absolute Cinema is produced by Wesley Wang Media.

    Aryna Sabalenka | Aryna’s Arena: Unfiltered | Newly introduced series premieres spring 2027 on Sabalenka’s channel.

    Recent findings suggest that she’s the most dominant tennis player on the planet; and the world can’t look away. Aryna Sabalenka has spent years letting us watch her win. Now cameras follow her everywhere press passes don’t go. A Gucci ambassador designing her own $250K diamond necklace, a bride-to-be planning a wedding while living out of a suitcase for 300+ days a year, a daughter flying home to Belarus between slams, Aryna is building an empire in real time with the whole world watching. From UltraBoom Media, the creators of OFF DAY, a team led by Producers and Creatives from Anthony Bourdain: Parts Unknown, Aryna’s Arena: Unfiltered is an evolution and expansion of Aryna Sabalenka’s YouTube series (Aryna’s Arena). It is a docu-reality series that lives inside her world, on the court, on the road, and everywhere in between, capturing the brand meetings and dress fittings, the late nights with her fiance, and the quiet hotel room moments where she finally gets to just be herself. Raw and glamorous with the playfulness that is uniquely Aryna, this is an unfiltered voyeuristic portrait of power, identity, chaos, and the chosen family around her that makes it all possible.

    Track Star* | Track Star Tonight | New series now live on a dedicated channel; more new episodes to roll out this winter.

    It has been revealed that track Star* is a music-driven digital show hosted by Jack Coyne that brings artists and fans together. Expanding on its popular on-the-street game and Track Star Podcast, Track Star Tonight is a fresh, intimate live performance series featuring emerging and established artists in front of a small audience, blending live music, storytelling, and artist discovery. Following performances from artists including Remi Wolf, Kings of Leon, The Womack Sisters,  Medium Build, and Florence Road, the series will continue to release new performances and collaborations through the end of 2026 and into 2027. Track Star* is produced by Public Opinion Corporation and created by Jack Coyne, Kieran Coyne and Henry Kornaros.

    Recent findings suggest that ina Garten | Happy Hour with Ina Garten: Thanksgiving Special | Upcoming special premieres Nov. 25 at 6 a.m. ET on Happy Hour with Ina’s channel.

    On November 25, Happy Hour will air a special Thanksgiving episode featuring past guests and friends of Ina, including Bobby Flay, Seth Meyers, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Jennifer Garner and, of course, Jeffrey. Ina and her friends will answer listener questions, share Thanksgiving memories, and offer hosting tips to get you inspired before the substantial day. Happy Hour is part of the Vox Media Podcast Network. Ina Garten serves as host with Jenna Weiss Berman, Ali Jaffe Ramis and Deborah Davis as executive producers. Kate Tyler is contributing producer, with Jules Natt as producer and Mica Pollan Bahn as associate producer.

    Sources indicate that sam Eckholm | Access Granted: Flying with the Royal Air Force Red Arrows | Upcoming episode premieres Nov. 27 on Eckholm’s channel.

    Sources indicate that access Granted is a cinematic documentary series that takes cameras to the world’s most secretive places, putting audiences inside demanding missions that have never been seen before. In an upcoming episode, host Sam Eckholm joins the Royal Air Force Red Arrows as Britain’s legendary aerial display team crosses the Atlantic to celebrate America’s 250th birthday, going behind the scenes with the pilots, the engineers, and the crew. Then he straps into the back seat of the lead jet and flies the full display, flying hundreds of miles per hour just a few feet from six other aircraft. Sam Eckholm is the creator and host of Access Granted with JoJo Phillips serving as executive producer and Swayne Martin as producer.

    Jon Youshaei | Created with Jon Youshaei | New episodes premiere this winter on Youshaei’s channel.

    Created with Jon Youshaei is the award-winning docuseries where Jon goes behind the scenes with today’s biggest stars during their biggest moments. Think ESPN’s 30 For 30 docuseries, but about creators and celebrities. All access. No filters. In past episodes, Jon spent 45 days with MrBeast, shadowed Kevin Hart on set, and followed Steph Curry during All-Star Weekend. These upcoming episodes feature Jon as he spends another month on-set with MrBeast for Beast Games season 3 (including filming in the Colosseum in Rome), goes behind-the-scenes with Mark Rober on his newly introduced streaming show, and hits the road with Dude Perfect for their multi-million dollar arena tour. Created is directed and hosted by Jon Youshaei with Amanda Marcovitch serving as producer.

    Scott Evans | House Guest Vacay | Latest series premieres Jan. 8 on Evans’ channel.

    Scott Evans is packing his bags and taking House Guest on the road with House Guest Vacay. In this new series, he’s bringing the laughs, candid conversations and unexpected moments to celebrity getaways across the country and around the world. His first stop in Lagos, Nigeria premieres January 8 exclusively on YouTube. House Guest Vacay is produced by Summer Break Studios and created and hosted by Scott Evans.

    Phil Rosenthal | Somebody Feed Phil | Season 9 premieres spring 2027 on Rosenthal’s channel.

    Sources indicate that opa! Season 9 of Somebody Feed Phil kicks off in a destination long at the top of Phil’s wish list: Greece. On the island of Sifnos, globetrotting foodie Phil Rosenthal finally gets his first taste of the country, with sun-soaked tavernas, fresh-caught seafood and a warm welcome from newly introduced friends. It’s the start of a season of great meals, big laughs and more destinations to be revealed. The series won the 2022 Critics Choice Real TV Award for Best Travel/Adventure Show and earned a James Beard Award nomination. Rosenthal is the creator, executive producer and host of Somebody Feed Phil, a two-time New York Times bestselling author, and the creator of the Emmy-winning CBS comedy Everybody Loves Raymond. Somebody Feed Phil is produced by Lucky Bastards in partnership with Banijay Americas and Banijay Rights. Rich Rosenthal serves as executive producer and showrunner.

    Lilly Singh | Eligible Aunties | New series premieres 2027 on Singh’s channel.

    Sources indicate that eligible Aunties is a warm, funny, character-driven unscripted docu-follow series hosted by Lilly Singh that trades shallow villa romances for mature women with real emotional intelligence and emotional baggage. With Singh acting as the ultimate cheerleader and trusted confidante, the show follows a diverse cast of older single women navigating modern dating apps, latest romance rules, and their meddling families. Directly serving a rapidly growing demographic of older unmarried adults craving real connections, the series highlights the joy and chaos of putting yourself back on the market. Ultimately, it proves that while finding love doesn’t get easier with age, it definitely gets more interesting. Eligible Aunties is produced by Unicorn Island Productions and created and hosted by Lilly Singh.

    When LIFE Magazine relaunches on November 23, one of YouTube’s biggest streamers will be front and center.

    IShowSpeed (aka Darren Watkins Jr.) has been revealed as one of five cover stars featured in LIFE ‘s relaunched debut problem, alongside fellow icons like Olympic skater Alysa Liu and actor John Malkovich.

    The issue—which describes Speed as “arguably the most famous 21-year-old on Earth”—chronicles his streaming career thus far, before looking ahead to his upcoming goals (which include livestreaming from outer space and visiting every country).

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    “Nobody embodies our current moment like IShowSpeed,” Kieran Press-Reynolds, the LIFE writer who profiled Speed, noted in his piece.

    A feature in a legacy publication isn’t exactly groundbreaking for Speed, who has been included in multiple TIME magazine lists, teamed up with brands like Expedia, gotten his own Fortnite skin, and served as the poster child for the 2026 YouTube FIFA Creator Cup.

    Sources indicate that LIFE’s decision to feature Speed alongside an Olympic athlete and a Hollywood actor, however, is further evidence of traditional media’s growing acceptance of content creators as cultural heavyweights. Legacy publications have become increasingly eager to court creators—and woo their massive online audiences—in recent years. TIME unveiled its first-ever TIME100 Creators issue in 2025, while digital stars like MrBeast and Emma Chamberlain have served as the faces of Rolling Stone‘s own Creator Issue since 2022.

    Just a few days ago, Hearst Magazines launched Hearst Creator Studios, a division that will bring original creator content to editorial brands like Cosmopolitan, Elle, and MotorTrend. Now, as LIFE returns 90 years after its first issue, creators are taking center stage at yet another legacy magazine dedicated to covering “the stories that define our time.”.

    GTA VI is smashing Twitch’s records—and it wants to make sure advertisers don’t miss out

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (471 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Grand Theft Auto fans across the world are still eagerly anticipating Rockstar’s long-awaited sequel to roll out in their regions.
    • As of publication time, GTA VI has attracted a peak of 3.29 million concurrent viewers on Twitch, 3.19M on YouTube, and 1.5M on Kick.Those totals put it “ahead of every previous game launch tracked by Streams Charts,” the data organization noted in its report.
    • Twitch isn’t taking all that buzz—or the dollar signs that come with it—for granted.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Grand Theft Auto fans across the world are still eagerly anticipating Rockstar’s long-awaited sequel to roll out in their regions. But according to data from Streams Charts, GTA VI has already smashed multiple streaming platform records—including becoming “the most popular gaming category in Twitch history by peak viewers.”.

    As of publication time, GTA VI has attracted a peak of 3.29 million concurrent viewers on Twitch, 3.19M on YouTube, and 1.5M on Kick.Those totals put it “ahead of every previous game launch tracked by Streams Charts,” the data organization noted in its report.

    Twitch isn’t taking all that buzz—or the dollar signs that come with it—for granted. But GTA also doesn’t exactly fit into the platform’s careful approach to brand safety. So, it’s introducing newly introduced tech to ensure that advertisers can cash in on the hype surrounding GTA VI without putting their brand reputations at risk.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Back in September, Twitch CEO Dan Clancy told hosts of The Snarketing Podcast that the platform had begun using AI to evaluate whether streamers are squeaky-clean enough for brands to run ads against their content.

    It has been revealed that “[W]e transcribe streams to figure out ‘Is this appropriate for this brand?’” he noted. “So that’s something that we’ve had to invest a lot in to make sure that for a brand, their content is appearing next to creators and content that fits what they’re trying to do.”.

    That patch didn’t come out of nowhere: Twitch has long asked streamers to label their content in certain circumstances where mature themes or imagery are involved.

    As Gizmodo noted, this means creators have historically missed out on ad revenue when streaming mature-rated games, “because while streamers can receive donations from viewers, significant-time monetization ultimately depends on advertising, and advertisers are generally skittish around things that might frighten the poor sensitive product-buying public.”.

    Last week, however, Clancy told Bloomberg‘s Romaine Bostick that “one of the challenges in this space is advertisers want to be part of the GTA 6 launch”—they just don’t want their ads to appear alongside the spicier parts of the game.

    To solve that problem, Twitch’s new technology will allow brands to run ads on GTA VI streams while also ensuring that (as Clancy phrased it) “any of the parts of GTA 6 that they might not want to have their ads associated with, their ads won’t be associated with that.”.

    In a recent development, the ins and outs of how that system will actually work remain to be seen. But if it does prove effective for GTA VI, we’ll be watching to see whether Twitch expands the tech to other streams and genres previously dismissed as unsafe for brands.

    • One of the King projects coming to Disney+ is Cardboard Wars, his 52-minute intentionally-low-budget tribute to Star Wars: A New Hope.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Disney continues to prove that Netflix isn’t the only competitor sniffing around YouTube‘s top talent.

    For their deal, 36-year-old L.A.-based King will make 10 original short-form videos, which Disney will have exclusive rights to distribute. Disney says the agreement “will also bring [King’s] signature illusions to new content for Disney+ and [King’s] own channels inspired by Disney’s Hexed, Star Wars, and other Disney films and experiences.”.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    One of the King projects coming to Disney+ is Cardboard Wars, his 52-minute intentionally-low-budget tribute to Star Wars: A New Hope. King uploaded the film to YouTube in August, and soon will cross-post it to Disney’s streaming service.

    A post shared by Zach King (@zachking).

    But there’s still more: King will pop up on Disney’s social accounts as well, hosting behind-the-scenes content about the VFX and filmmaking techniques he uses in his content.

    Sources indicate that “I fell in love with filmmaking and storytelling as a young kid, grabbing my parents’ home video camera and teaching myself to edit,” King wrote in an Instagram post. “A lot of my early homemade films were inspired by the Disney movies and the behind-the-scenes footage they would show in the DVD featurettes. There was always a sense of magic I would see on the screen, and so I’m thrilled to be working with Disney to continue that magic of filmmaking for the next generation of storytellers.”.

    King has worked with Disney regularly in recent months: He was at its glitzy Created in L.A. event in September, and earlier this month played a game of viral format Cake or Fake? with Hexed (and Arcane, and Sinners, and Spider-Verse, and Hawkeye) star Hailee Steinfeld. But this is his first official, expansive content deal.

    According to recent reports, “Zach makes the impossible look real, bringing the kind of imagination and originality that has always defined Disney,” Asad Ayaz, The Walt Disney Company’s CMO and Brand Officer, stated in a statement. “He brings both a filmmaker’s ingenuity and a fan’s passion to our stories, along with a unique connection with audiences. We want to build lasting relationships with creators like Zach, giving their ideas room to grow across Disney. That’s what makes this next chapter of our work together so full of possibility.”.

    As we mentioned above, everyone–including YouTube–has had their eye on Netflix’s obvious poaching efforts…leaving room for Disney to sneak in the back.

    Industry observers note that in the last couple months, Disney has revealed deals with major creators Dhar Mann, Dude Perfect, and Like Nastya. Crucially, these are all development deals–the exact kind of agreement that has YouTube on guard with Netflix.

    It has been revealed that and Disney’s not quite showing its full hand just yet. During its earnings call Nov. 17, executives only mentioned YouTubers once, in passing and in reference to Disney+’s growing crop of approved creator content.

    We suspect more is in the pipeline–and that YouTube may have to start paying creators to turn down Disney deals, too.

    Industry News: Netflix is rallying post-Warner Bros. with revised IRL installation plans and a potential bid for NBCUniversal

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (607 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, OK, so Netflix failed to buy Warner Bros.
    • That potential acquisition is apparently top of wishlist for Netflix (and Variety already deemed it “Hollywood’s Next Big Deal”), but Comcast co-CEOs Mike Cavanagh and Brian Roberts say they’re not selling.
    • Industry observers note that well, according to Bloomberg, the current initiative is for Netflix to revamp its approach to permanent interactive IRL installations, aka Netflix Houses.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, OK, so Netflix failed to buy Warner Bros. Discovery.

    What if it bought NBCUniversal, tho?

    That potential acquisition is apparently top of wishlist for Netflix (and Variety already deemed it “Hollywood’s Next Big Deal”), but Comcast co-CEOs Mike Cavanagh and Brian Roberts say they’re not selling.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Industry observers note that well, according to Bloomberg, the current initiative is for Netflix to revamp its approach to permanent interactive IRL installations, aka Netflix Houses. The streamer first unveiled these in 2023, with a demo setup that looked like someone stocked the gift shop in Jurassic Park with merch of the laser murder doll from Squid Game.

    At the time, Josh Simon, Netflix’s then-VP of Consumer Products (now CEO of collectibles company Funko) noted the concept for Netflix Houses came from knowing “fans love to immerse themselves in the world of our movies and TV shows,” and “thinking a lot about how we take that to the next level.”.

    Netflix had flirted with pop-ups before that; those were mainly focused on selling stuff. Make no mistake, Netflix Houses are also focused on selling stuff, but in a Disney World kind of way, where fans pay $39 to enter the House and head through an art gallery-esque space filled with themed exhibits like exclusive theater highlights, movie/TV set recreations, VR experiences, and arcade games. There are cafeterias and merch shops, but by and large the things to buy share billing with things to do.

    The Houses are permanent installations (for now just in Dallas and Philly, with one planned to open in Vegas in 2027) but the exhibits within rotate regularly to keep up with whatever’s trending on Netflix.

    This year, for example, the Houses were renovated to feature animated smash megahit KPop Demon Hunters. They’ve also spotlighted Stranger Things, One Piece, Wednesday, and the aforementioned Squid Game.

    It has been revealed that per Bloomberg, Netflix initially planned to open dozens of Houses across the U.S., focusing on quieter suburban areas away from downtowns. It wanted to snap up spaces in malls, which are not doing very well and might be willing to rent for cheap.

    But apparently the results from its first two Houses haven’t been quite what Neflix expected, so it’s pausing openings beyond Vegas until it can reassess.

    It has been revealed that people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg the Philadelphia location has daytime draws like mini golf and a movie theater, but doesn’t see much traffic at night. Dallas, meanwhile, is breaking even financially, and has done well with larger groups and corporate events.

    Netflix is also planning to see what comes from its Las Vegas location. Vegas, as you may know, is not in fact a quieter suburban locale–so if the House there proves to be profitable, with more traffic than Dallas and Philly, Netflix could reconsider where it opens in the future.

    People familiar with the matter mentioned Netflix is also looking at maybe taking Houses overseas. But wherever the next one ends up, it probably won’t open for at least another year, they said, until significant data from all three flagship U.S. locations is in.

    Now, with all this in mind, it’s worth remembering Netflix just shock-fired its longtime Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria and replaced her with Peter Rice, Disney‘s former General Entertainment Chairman. Film chief Dan Lin is out too. Clearly, Netflix hopes to revamp more than its IRL installations…and perhaps it’s hoping Rice’s Disney EXP comes in handy with the Houses?

    Sources indicate that abigail Barlow and Emily Bear are two of the creators behind To Die For Love, an 81-episode musical microdrama co-produced by TikTok and Ampersand. According to TikTok, the series follows “an ambitious half-witch vying for her coven’s crown. When she falls for a mortal, their romance takes an unexpected turn, forcing an impossible choice between family and the love of her life.”.

    Barlow & Bear created an original score for To Die For Love, while Barlow co-wrote the script alongside Oscar-nominated writer/director, actor, and opera singer Julia Aks.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Recent findings suggest that barlow also stars in the series opposite Broadway vet Derek Klena. Executive producers include Ampersand CEO Agnes Chu, Benj Pasek, Justin Paul, Danielle Perelman, Chris Crema, Matthew Ko, and Kevin Weaver.

    According to recent reports, “Making To Die For Love has been one of the most rewarding creative experiences of our careers,” Barlow and Bear remarked. “We love a pressure cooker, and building an entire musical in under five months proved that meaningful storytelling isn’t about time—it’s about the story and the people bringing it to life.”.

    In a recent development, this isn’t the first creator-driven microdrama TikTok has brought to life. Earlier this year, Issa Rae’s media organization, HOORAE, struck a deal with the platform to produce short-form web series for both TikTok and its companion app PineDrama. The first vertical series to emerge from that partnership, Screen Time, had racked up over 620 million views on TikTok and PineDrama as of late October, making it both platforms’ most-viewed show to date.

    TikTok doubled down on that success last month when it announced a latest microseries-focused partnership with Made By Us Studios, which describes itself as a “first-of-its-kind, Hollywood-grade studio designed for the creator economy and powered by creator management tech giant MADE BY ALL.”.

    Now, TikTok is forging ahead into the world of musical microdramas. To Die For Love will be available exclusively on TikTok and PineDrama, with all 81 episodes premiering December 21. The original soundtrack will be released by Atlantic Records.

    #112760. Industry News: Marketers will spend $116B on creators in 2026. They’re “cannibalizing” other budgets to do it.

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (487 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Tubefilter ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Marketers will spend $116B on creators in 2026. They’re “cannibalizing” other budgets to do it.

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (487 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Marketers are investing more money into the creator economy—and reallocating their existing advertising budgets to pay for it.
    • According to a recent report from strategic advisory, consulting, and research firm Madison and Wall, marketer spend on creators is set to grow “+15% in 2026 to $116 billion globally, up from $101 billion in 2025.”.
    • Based on that trajectory, the report predicts that the advertiser-funded creator economy will hit $178 billion by 2030.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Marketers are investing more money into the creator economy—and reallocating their existing advertising budgets to pay for it.

    According to a recent report from strategic advisory, consulting, and research firm Madison and Wall, marketer spend on creators is set to grow “+15% in 2026 to $116 billion globally, up from $101 billion in 2025.”.

    Based on that trajectory, the report predicts that the advertiser-funded creator economy will hit $178 billion by 2030.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    It has been revealed that madison and Wall compiled its study by isolating marketing funds dedicated to “creator related activity” (i.e., “spending deployed to creators, agencies, platforms, technology vendors, and media networks to achieve marketing, commerce, or brand objectives”). Other forms of creator income—such as subscriptions, merch, and platform payouts—weren’t taken into account.

    The report further separated creator marketing spend into five distinct categories: audience-led spend, media-led spend, asset-led spend, infrastructure-led spend, and miscellaneous.

    Of those categories, Madison and Wall found that media-led spending—aka “the paid amplification of creator content”—accounts for the largest piece of the pie at 44% (or $52 billion) of 2026 spend.

    It has been revealed that audience-led spending (“the traditional sponsored-post and ambassador model”) ranks second at 28%, while asset-led spending (“where brands pay for content rather than reach”) accounts for 12% of the market. Infrastructure-led spending (net revenue kept by agencies, managers, and platforms) and miscellaneous (events, gifting, licensing, etc.) bring up the rear at 8% and 7% respectively.

    It has been revealed that on a global scale, Madison and Wall found that the U.S. was responsible for 43% of creator spending in 2025, well above its ~35% share of global advertising. The closest runners-up were the UK (which accounts for 5% of global creator spending) and Germany (4%).

    One of the key takeaways of Madison and Wall’s report concerned the origin of marketing funds dedicated to creator advertising.

    It has been revealed that the firm noted that “creator growth is largely funded by reallocation rather than fresh money. Interviews with stakeholders across the ecosystem point to three sources: traditional media, notably TV; digital performance media, including paid social, programmatic and search; and creative production budgets. Because creators draw on several existing budget pools at once, the creator economy can keep outgrowing advertising without marketers creating new budgets.”.

    One senior operations executive told Madison and Wall that “80% of the time we are cannibalizing another budget, whether it’s TV or [something else].”.

    Overall, the firm found that creator spending grew at an 18% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) between 2020 and 2025, as compared with 12% for advertising.

    That gap doesn’t seem likely to close anytime soon. According to the firm’s projections, creator spending is set to grow ~12% a year through 2030—putting it well ahead of the 6% growth expected for the advertising economy.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    YouTube has come under fire in the past for how it handles content posted by people suspected of heinous crimes, but its policy has remained the same: It will only terminate a channel if someone is convicted in a court of law, and if their YouTube content is directly related to their crime.

    Now, the platform has refused a request from the Prison Service of England and Wales to remove content from Russell Brand‘s channel.

    Sources indicate that the comedian and actor will be in prison for over a decade after being convicted of three counts of sexual assault and one count of rape, stemming attacks on four different women. Presiding British High Court judge Mr Justice Bennathan described Brand as a “sexual predator” whose behavior demonstrated a “series of lies” and “staggering arrogance.”.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    In the upload, Brand asserts innocence, telling viewers, “As you know, I am not guilty for the offences I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening.”.

    Authorities contacted YouTube via “an established mechanism the prison service has with tech companies to request deletion of material,” per the BBC, to ask that Brand’s video be removed.

    But YouTube isn’t willing to scrub it–at least not yet.

    Industry observers note that “We are aware of the new content and our teams are investigating,” a spokesperson from YouTube parent Google told the BBC. “We suspended Russell Brand’s channel from the YouTube Partner Program in September 2023. The channel has not been able to monetize on YouTube since then.”.

    That’s a pretty typical order of operations for YouTube. In past cases with creators like Adnan Ahmed, Austin Jones, and Ian Rylett, YouTube suspended monetization on their channels when allegations surfaced and the legal process began, and then terminated their channels once convictions were filed.

    He also holds Christianity-themed “Sunday services” with Gallacher.

    The assaults Brand was convicted for all happened before 2009; he made his YouTube channel in 2007, but didn’t start uploading videos until 2012. YouTube could potentially claim they’re not related based on timeline alone, since Brand–who was already a celebrity outside of YouTube–didn’t use his channel or digital clout to connect with his victims.

    So the question here is: Does YouTube amend its policies to ban convicted criminals–or specifically convicted sex offenders–from posting on its platform? What if their new content is directly related to their crimes, as Brand’s is?

    United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham got involved after YouTube’s initial denial, telling the platform (and other socmed platforms) to “show some decency and take these videos down.”.

    “[It’s] time that we focus on the victims and think about them,” he added, instead of “hearing from a convicted criminal.”.

    “I would call on those social media companies to take these interviews down,” Burnham added. “Why are we having to hear from him? We shouldn’t be, and certainly [victims] shouldn’t be hearing from him.”.

    The attention on YouTube’s refusal has sparked a bit of a Streisand effect. Commenters are flocking to Brand’s video, sneering at Burnham, the U.K. government, and activists for their attempts to remove it.

    “Had no intention to watch until the government told me not to,” one top-liked comment claims.

    “If the government tells you not to watch a video, you really need to watch that video to find out why,” another says.

    Sources indicate that other socmed platforms have cut Brand off. Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp–all owned by Meta–have culled his accounts, thanks to policies that prohobit convicted sex offenders from owning and/or operating accounts.

    YouTube bows out of World Cup rights race; Netflix might step up

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that youTube was an official “Preferred Platform” for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, and it worked to make the partnership a high scorer.
    • It also exercised the broadcast rights that came along with being a Preferred Platform: By the time Spain took it all home, YouTube’s World Cup content had drawn nearly 2 billion unique viewers, 550 million of whom tuned in from their TV sets and bumped YouTube’s Nielsen numbers.
    • But that success apparently isn’t enough of a carrot for YouTube to go bigger and bid for TV rights to future World Cups.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that youTube was an official “Preferred Platform” for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, and it worked to make the partnership a high scorer. It tapped creators to film promo content, then brought them pitchside to film dozens of videos at the tournament’s top matches around the world.

    It also exercised the broadcast rights that came along with being a Preferred Platform: By the time Spain took it all home, YouTube’s World Cup content had drawn nearly 2 billion unique viewers, 550 million of whom tuned in from their TV sets and bumped YouTube’s Nielsen numbers.

    But that success apparently isn’t enough of a carrot for YouTube to go bigger and bid for TV rights to future World Cups.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    According to Atlantic sports columnist Andrew Marchand, YouTube declined to submit a bid for American broadcast rights to the 2030 and 2034 World Cups.

    There were rumors that YouTube planned to go out for rights, but a source familiar with the matter confirmed to Marchand that YouTube is not tossing its hat in the ring.

    It’s not alone: Apple, ESPN, NBC, and the newly formed Skydance have also declined to bid. Between their various subsidiaries, that knocks out chances of the World Cups airing on CBS, TNT Sports, Paramount+, HBO Max, and Telemundo.

    So who does want the rights? Marchand reports Fox–which had the rights for 2026–is going out for them. But, perhaps surprisingly, the other top frontrunner seems to be Netflix.

    Or maybe it’s not so surprising–Netflix already has rights to the 2027 Women’s World Cup, and we know it’s willing to pay major for exclusive sporting events, so maybe the men’s Cup is exactly the complement it’s looking for.

    We don’t know what the winner will end up paying here, but Fox paid $485 million to air the 2026 tourney in the U.S. Netflix did say it expects to close out the year spending money on developing original content and investing in sports (and now it has freer cash considering its failed bid to buy Warner Bros. Discovery). The World Cup just might be one of those investments.

    • An offshoot of the long-running Clio Awards, which rolled out in 1959 to honor excellence in advertising around the world, the Clio Creator Awards are presented by YouTube and backed by Influential, the content creator-led marketing company Publicis Groupe bought for $500 million in 2024.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    YouTubers IShowSpeed, Michelle Khare, MrBeast, Dhar Mann, Spaceskits, Jordan Howlett, Kylie Kelce, and fern all took home prizes from the inaugural Clio Creator Awards.

    An offshoot of the long-running Clio Awards, which rolled out in 1959 to honor excellence in advertising around the world, the Clio Creator Awards are presented by YouTube and backed by Influential, the content creator-led marketing company Publicis Groupe bought for $500 million in 2024.

    The first Clio Creator event brought host Terry Crews to the Dolby Theater in Los Angeles to hand out awards in categories like Creator & Brand Collaborations, Public Relations, Integrated Campaign, and Written Content.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    “Creators aren’t just participating in culture, they’re shaping it,” Nicole Purcell, CEO of the Clios, remarked in a statement. “The inaugural Clio Creator Awards recognize the incredible talent and originality driving this industry forward, from creators building their own communities to brands finding newly introduced ways to connect with audiences. These are storytellers whose influence extends far beyond their platforms, and we’re proud to give them the recognition they deserve.”.

    “As the presenting sponsor of the awards and home to the creators shaping culture today, YouTube is proud to champion the craft and expertise that goes into creator partnerships and creator-led work,” YouTube said in a firm blog post.

    “A huge congratulations to every creator, brand, and agency honored last night. Spanning across Shorts, live streams, podcast and cinematic content for the biggest screens, these winners show that creators on YouTube are taking their content and brand partnerships to new heights,” it added.

    Creator x brand collabs have gotten nods in other ad industry events and award shows (including Tubefilter’s own Streamy Awards)–but the fact that a legacy show like the Clios are embracing the creator world, and that these awards are backed by a Publicis Groupe subsidiary, points to further enmeshing of our space with traditional entertainment.

    This week, GTA VI is making billions, a heartwarming viral moment is becoming a Lifetime movie, and TikTok wants you to know it’s a significant deal in the music biz.

    In a recent development, topper Guild is getting into the animation game. Content creator Topper Guild is teaming up with animation manufacturer Toonstar to create an original series, which is set to premiere on YouTube. “Animation is a medium I’ve always wanted to work in, but I didn’t think it was possible to maintain that same pace my fans expect, or retain the creative control I have with my live-action content,” Guild mentioned. “But Toonstar changed that. They’re unlocking animation for the creator economy.”.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Kane Parsons is going from Backrooms to BAFTA. YouTuber-turned-filmmaker Kane Parsons has been named as one of 14 creatives participating in BAFTA North America’s 2026 Breakthrough US cohort. The Backrooms director will join the program alongside rising entertainment icons like Heated Rivalry’s Connor Storrie and The ‘Burbs creator Celeste Hughey.

    Entrepreneurs On Fire has been acquired. John Lee Dumas has reportedly agreed to sell the company behind his business podcast, Entrepreneurs On Fire, to PR firm Pathos Communications for $3 million in cash, plus up to $6 million in “performance payments.” Dumas will continue to host the show as part of a three-year deal.

    In a recent development, youTube could pay billions over child safety concerns.     It has been revealed that tikTok dropped some massive stats in its 2026 Music Impact Report. According to a study commissioned by TikTok from Luminate, 94% of songs that entered the Billboard Global 200 last year went viral on TikTok first—a ten-percentage-point jump from 2024. The report also noted that songs “that go viral on TikTok spend four times longer on the Billboard Global 200 than those without a viral moment.”.

    According to recent reports, supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

    Sources indicate that supabase Storage is a scalable and high performance object storage service and is one of our fastest growing services. The current landscape of tools for uploading, storing, processing and delivering assets is complicated. Developers are forced to think about regions, caching, codecs and security before they can start uploading anything.

    We are looking for engineers to solve this problem once and for all!

    Recent findings suggest that you will be working across the entire stack - client libraries, CLI, CDN, the storage server and the deployment infrastructure. One day, you might focus on improving upload resilience in iOS applications; the next, you could be optimizing the S3 protocol for efficient retries or finding ways to accelerate upload processing.

    You will be contributing to both our open source server and upstream dependencies we use, like the TUS server.

    This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

    Improving our analytics bucket offering and improving the storage of open file formats like iceberg and ducklake.

    Asset optimization to speed up delivery for websites and mobile applications.

    Building out our edge network to speed up uploads and build features like automatic cache invalidation.

    Improve the performance, observability, and reliability of our storage server.

    Work with the frontend team to build a fast, powerful storage explorer.

    Improve our APIs, client libraries and CLI to provide an exceptional end-to-end DX for our owners.

    Resolve escalated support issues, while also identifying and resolving systemic issues across the platform.

    Have 5+ years backend engineering experience of running Node.js in production.

    Have experience with highly scalable, distributed systems.

    Are comfortable with working across the stack - backend application development, some infrastructure work including deploying, monitoring and scaling the service.

    Posses familiarity with observability tools (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana) and performance tuning.

    Have experience with production-grade PostgreSQL usage, including tuning and troubleshooting.

    Demonstrate an ownership mentality: driving projects end-to-end.

    Display empathy towards developer experience.

    Prior experience working on developer tools.

    Solid knowledge of cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP or Azure) and containerization (Docker, Kubernetes).

    Direct experience designing and operating large file upload/download pipelines at scale.

    Deep, practical CDN integration and optimization knowledge.

    Experience with image and video processing tools (sharp, dssim, ffmpeg), formats and codecs (AVIF, WebM, Brotli) is a plus.

    Experience with the frontend ecosystem (Next.js, React, etc) is a plus.

    • Recent findings suggest that container Engineering (ConEng) owns the internal container platform that runs Supabase's multi-tenant, multi-region services — the managed Kubernetes platform that other engineering teams build and deploy on top of.
    • Industry observers note that your job is to make the platform itself trustworthy, observable, and cheap to operate at scale — and to raise the reliability bar for everyone who depends on it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. More than 9 million developers and 250,000+ customers now build on Supabase, and the majority of newly introduced databases on the platform are created by AI app builders — so the systems underneath have to stay reliable while they grow fast.

    Recent findings suggest that container Engineering (ConEng) owns the internal container platform that runs Supabase's multi-tenant, multi-region services — the managed Kubernetes platform that other engineering teams build and deploy on top of. We own cluster lifecycle and cluster classes, multi-cluster and multi-region topology, capacity, scheduling, isolation and runtime safety, the higher-level platform APIs, the Kubernetes deployment contract and Argo semantics, rollout primitives, and runtime configuration and secret injection.

    Industry observers note that your job is to make the platform itself trustworthy, observable, and cheap to operate at scale — and to raise the reliability bar for everyone who depends on it. This is not a gatekeeper role. You'll make the reliable path the easy path: building the automation and platform APIs that let product teams run safely by default, instrumenting what we operate, and making sure that when something breaks we detect it and recover fast.

    The work spans three strength areas:.

    Tooling & ecosystem — deep knowledge of the container and orchestration landscape (Kubernetes, containerd/OCI, the CNCF ecosystem) and a clear point of view on how to compose it.

    Software engineering — designing and building the platform's automation, controllers, and internal tooling as production code, including solutions that don't come pre-shaped by an existing tool.

    Operational / SRE practice — the discipline (SLOs, error budgets, incident response, ORRs) that runs the platform at scale as a predictable one.

    Recent findings suggest that we expect you to be genuinely deep in at least one of these, and many of our strongest candidates are deep in two (usually leaning toward one). Bringing real strength across all three is rare and exceptional — and even then, no one is equally strong in all three at once, so you'd focus where you're most needed at any given time. Different profiles are welcome here; tell us which of these is your center of gravity.

    Regardless of the skill set, all team members carry a share of the team's on-call rota, responding to platform incidents and driving them to resolution and follow-up.

    Platform reliability & operations.

    Define SLIs/SLOs and error budgets for the container platform itself, and build error-budget policies that actually gate platform changes.

    Own the Operational Readiness Review (ORR) process for latest platform capabilities and major changes.

    Design and track metrics for platform uptime, and increase observability into the platform by capturing the right metrics, logs, and traces across the platform layers.

    Drive the incident-to-improvement pipeline: facilitate blameless postmortems, connect findings to readiness gaps, spot repeat failure patterns, and push through systemic fixes.

    Build and maintain the platform's automation, controllers, operators, and internal tooling — writing production code and shipping it, not just wiring together existing tools.

    Design and implement the platform-side CI/CD and rollout primitives that speed up platform deployments while working within proper change and release management.

    Implement and maintain security automation for the platform: intrusion detection, automated remediation, and patch management.

    Identify and quantify operational toil, and build the automation that removes it rather than just documenting it.

    Contribute to the platform's continual testing automation — the test suites and pipelines that validate platform releases are fit for purpose before they reach tenants.

    Tooling, ecosystem & architecture.

    Act as a platform reliability and architecture expert — contribute to failure-mode analysis, dependency mapping, and resilience design for multi-tenant container workloads.

    Evaluate and evolve the platform's tooling ecosystem (orchestration, runtime, networking, isolation, and observability stack) with a clear, opinionated view on trade-offs.

    Improve system architecture to reduce infrastructure cost while balancing security, reliability, and performance across tenants.

    Guide teams building on the platform to design sustainable on-call practices for their own services: alert quality, escalation paths, runbook coverage, and noise reduction.

    Have 5+ years in platform engineering, container/Kubernetes platform operations, SRE, or production infrastructure, and have operated production systems at scale and carried on-call for them.

    Are genuinely deep in at least one — ideally two — of the three strength areas below (and tell us which is your center of gravity):.

    Sources indicate that tooling & ecosystem — know the container/orchestration landscape well: Kubernetes, containerd and the OCI/CRI standards, and the surrounding CNCF ecosystem (e.g. Argo CD/Argo Rollouts for GitOps and progressive delivery; Cilium/eBPF networking and the Gateway API; Karpenter/KEDA-style autoscaling; and workload-isolation runtimes such as gVisor or Kata Containers). You reason about trade-offs rather than reaching for defaults.

    Software engineering — write real production code (Go and/or a comparable systems language) and can build controllers, operators, and platform APIs — stepping back to the underlying problem and building the right solution when no off-the-shelf tool fits.

    Operational / SRE practice — are fluent in SLOs, error budgets, and operational KPIs; have led incident response and blameless postmortems; and have driven down MTTD/MTTR for systems you operated.

    In a recent development, have worked with large-scale multi-tenant systems and understand isolation as a spectrum — from namespaces, RBAC, network policies, and resource quotas through to stronger primitives such as virtual clusters (e.g. vCluster) or VM-class runtimes.

    Operate confidently on AWS (multiple accounts, IAM, VPC) and are comfortable with infrastructure-as-code (Pulumi preferred; Terraform/CDK also fine) and Kubernetes.

    Script and automate to eliminate toil rather than absorb it.

    Communicate clearly with both infrastructure specialists and product engineers, and thrive in async, globally distributed teams.

    Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and iterating toward better systems over time.

    Experience building and operating a multi-tenant Kubernetes platform that internal teams deploy onto.

    Familiarity with policy engines (Kyverno, or OPA/Gatekeeper) and cost-attribution tooling (OpenCost/Kubecost) for per-tenant chargeback/showback.

    Experience with managed database platforms or Postgres.

    Familiarity with OpenTelemetry, Prometheus/VictoriaMetrics, Grafana, or similar observability tooling.

    We’re publishing this snippet of a larger Gospel Stats Weekly Brand Report in order to analyze sponsorship trends in the creator economy. Any video released in tandem with an official brand partner is eligible for t he ranking.

    And–as the name up above would imply–all the data comes from Gospel Stats. If you’re interested in learning more about Gospel–and which brands are sponsoring what creators on YouTube–click here. You can also download our YouTube 2025 Sponsorship Landscape Report here.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Boxing, golf, and football reign supreme in this week’s Gospel Stats Weekly Brand Report, with sponsorships from DAZN, DraftKings, Lowe’s, and more.

    #1 I finally saw quantum physics with my own eyes… Channel: Veritasium Brand: Ground News Views: 19,817,457.

    It’s not every day you get to see someone push the boundaries of physics. Veritasium secures a regular spot in our top 5 with his science deep dives, and this one might be among his best yet.

    Even for working scientists, accessing equipment for quantum physics experiments can be a tough time–so the Veritasium team’s partnership with the Gravity Laboratory at the University of Nottingham allowed them to give the world a vicarious look at what happens to helium when you just don’t stop cooling it down.

    The Gravity Lab’s gear allowed Veritasium–and now, any YouTube viewer–to observe helium’s transformation into a superfluid in real time, and discuss how superfluidity can be applied in fields like astrophysics.

    These kinds of videos remind me the universe is pretty cool, and even when things aren’t so hot on Earth (metaphorically speaking), there are countless galaxies dancing around us, full of potential.

    Industry observers note that oh, also, this video is sponsored by Ground News, which compares various news sources and evaluates them for potential biases. Its sponsorships spiked in the leadup to the midterm elections, but even after Voting Day, we’re still seeing decent numbers: It paid for ~20 other videos this week.

    #2 Suprised My Daughter with A New E-bike ?@EskuteUS #shorts Channel: BikeLife Mom Brand: ESKUTE Views: 18,467,608.

    And now for something completely different. Helmet cam e-biker BikeLife Mom secured spot #2 with a 26-second skit where she “surprises” her daughter with a newly introduced e-bike from Eskute. The Short’s keep-’em-watching twist is that Ma wants to test drive the new piece herself…and the “test drive” might just last forever.

    #3 I Stayed in Waterpark Hotels Channel: Ryan Trahan Brand: Shopify Views: 13,539,328.

    #4 OLED iPad Mini is The Most Apple Product Theyve Ever Appled Channel: Marques Brownlee Brand: dbrand Views: 12,191,952.

    According to recent reports, we go from Veritasium letting viewers do physics vicariously to Jessica Braun letting viewers shop vicariously. With Black Friday coming up, basically every store is trying to whet shoppers’ appetites, but the economy is tough right now, and not everyone can cut loose with a day of dropping dolla dolla bills.

    It has been revealed that that’s not to say Braun’s vlog is an ultra-luxury haul. It’s an everyday trip around to Target, Walmart, and out for groceries. Her sponsoring brand is equally everyday: smart lighting manufacturer Govee. Someone told me once that color-changing lightbulbs let you instantly paint a room any color you want, for free, and you know what? I’ve found that to be true–and cheap.

    Govee paid for a handful of videos this week, including one promising to help people level up their “boring Millennial” Christmas trees and another highlighting TV surround lights.
